lines: MCP discovery requests structured effective-source metadata. Native contributions join `plugins.list` by their complete opaque `pluginId` (MCP uses `effectiveSource.plugin.id`), and plugin containers use the runtime-resolved `rootPath`. No ancestor manifest search, cache-layout inference, or plugin-directory rescan establishes ownership or adds undiscovered children. Missing inventory roots are not fabricated; hooks and MCP servers remain available in the standalone inventory. Discovery identities merge with live MCP connection state without duplicating servers. Observed SDK enablement supplies a non-persistent base for scoped host decisions, not a new host request to start or stop a server. Native inventory never supplies forwarded plugin directories, custom agent definitions, or MCP configurations.

+MCP tool routing includes enabled servers from passive `mcp.listConfigured` inventory, including SDK-discovered plugin and built-in servers without host-projected definitions. Routing search uses configured enablement and scoped host decisions independently of connection readiness, so unstarted and authentication-required servers remain discoverable; live tools supersede those proxies in tool search. Activation waits for the newest inventory refresh, including reads that supersede its own, before checking availability. SDK-only routing identities and tool metadata are not persisted in the shared configuration-keyed cache. Inventory and client-tool changes serialize SDK tool replacement, and routed-server metadata is published only after the SDK accepts the replacement.

Explicit native MCP disables are carried by the chat's customization snapshot into both create and resume gating, without forwarding definitions or projecting inherited SDK defaults as host intent. Runtime reconciliation restores both host-enabled and host-disabled servers to inheritance before relinquishing control. Confirmed external SDK configuration changes update the session's inherited default without persisting host decisions. Deduplication against explicit MCP declarations also filters nested SDK plugin children, preserving unrelated contributions.

If runtime MCP inventory arrives before SDK plugin discovery, keep the already-published live ID and reconcile the unique SDK-discovered child into it. Source metadata, inherited defaults, and the known plugin ownership must survive subsequent runtime updates; do not adopt unmarked or ambiguous same-name children, or overwrite a server whose runtime provenance identifies a non-plugin source.
